text:
sam: Heads up — found data from customer 'pi-labs' showing up in another workspace's Console view. Looks like a scoping bug in the dashboard filters. Screenshot attached :grimacing:
anya: uhoh. can you paste quick repro steps?
sam: repro: 1) Console -> Queries -> last 7d 2) Owner filter -> select 'engineering' 3) Observe rows where workspace == pi-labs (should be isolated). API response contains those rows.
mike: is this UI-side (filter bug) or backend returning cross-tenant data?
sam: backend. captured response payload includes entries with workspace_id=pi-labs for a different workspace's session id. sample log:```INFO 2026-05-03T12:56:10Z console-api request_id=req_9f8a path=/internal/console/query user=workspace-42 workspace_header=workspace-42 payload_count=120``````WARN 2026-05-03T12:56:10Z cache HIT key=console:queries:hash(xxx) cached_for=42ms tenant_key=NONE returned=15``` (notice tenant_key=NONE)
mike: that cache line is suspect. we recently changed the cache key composition to be query_hash + user_id but forgot tenant.
ara: tagging infra — if cache isn't namespacing by tenant, it's an obvious bleed. can you grep for tenant_key usage?
sam: yup grep shows console-api/lib/cache.js:``function cacheKey(req) { return `console:queries:${hash(req.query)}` } // no tenant header``
anya: yikes. what's the blast radius? production customers?
sam: saw it in EU prod, multiple customers queried the same owner filter, so probably others. I flagged it in logs where workspace_header was absent due to an older front-end client that omitted X-Workspace-Id on some AJAX calls.
mike: two vectors then: missing header from old client + cache key missing tenant namespace. both need fixes.
sentry-bot: New issue created: SENTRY-FF-3344 "console-api: cache returned cross-tenant rows" event.count=6 users=4 trace=tr_29fa
deploy-bot: Deploy queued: console-api v12.3.2 -> production (rolling)
anya: we should avoid full-prod rollout until we confirm fix. prefer canary in eu then rollback if needed.
mike: plan: 1) patch cacheKey to include workspace header fallback to req.session.workspace_id 2) also add server-side validation to reject requests without workspace header/session mismatch 3) push canary to eu region
sam: patch preview:```diff
- return `console:queries:${hash(req.query)}`
+ const tenant = req.headers['x-workspace-id'] || req.session?.workspace_id || 'unknown';
+ return `console:queries:${tenant}:${hash(req.query)}`
```
ara: also add a metric on cache_tenant_labels to catch future regressions.
mike: uploading PR: https://git.internal/redwood/console-api/pull/1246 (includes tests)
sam: test script i used:```curl -H "Authorization: Bearer token-for-ws-42" -H "X-Workspace-Id: ws-42" 'https://console.redwood.internal/internal/console/query?owner=engineering'``` then repeat with a different token and missing header to assert no mix.
anya: i'll open a priority ticket SYS-987: "audit console endpoints for tenant-scoped cache keys" and assign to eng-platform + eng-runtime.
mike: canary deploying patch to eu-canary now. monitor logs for tenant_key=NONE or cache HIT with mismatched workspace.
sentry-bot: Canary alert: identical event SENTRY-FF-3344 seen in eu-canary (count=1)
mike: investigating, looks like an edge case where legacy client still calling /internal/console/query without passing cookie/session properly. adding server-side strict reject for missing workspace header will be in PR.
sam: do we need to rollback?
mike: canary green for 10m, no cross-tenant rows observed after the cache key change. will continue monitoring for 30m before broader rollout.
deploy-bot: Canary passed gates, rolling to prod with 5% initially.
anya: good. please include a short postmortem stub in the ticket with root cause = cache key omitted tenant + legacy client that omitted workspace header; remediation = change cache key, add server-side validation, expand telemetry.
ara: also add an alert: sudden increase in cache hit ratio with tenant_key=NONE should page eng-platform.
sam: thanks everyone — PR merged, rollout underway. tagging customers we saw impacted and opening support threads. :white_check_mark:
mike: follow-up: run a job next week to reindex any cache entries created with tenant_key=NONE and invalidate them.
anya: agreed. we'll schedule postmortem and customer outreach.
sam: closing thread here — will paste postmortem once done.
